filename: Anomalous Meltwater From Ice Sheets and Ice Shelves Is a Historical Forcing.pdf
title: Anomalous Meltwater From Ice Sheets and Ice Shelves Is a Historical Forcing
processes: ice shelf basal melt and calving
regional and global sea level change
code_availability: The multi-model CMIP6 ensemble SST trend was produced on the LEAP-Pangeo portal using code archived at Busecke (2023, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8335419) and Busecke et al. (2023, xMIP, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7519179).
testbed_rationale: The study conducts traditional coupled GCM historical forcing experiments using GISS-E2.1-G without machine learning models, ML parameterization training, or dedicated ML benchmarks.
pain_points: Absence of dynamically coupled ice sheets and shelves in standard CMIP6 climate models requires treating meltwater as an ad-hoc external forcing.
Structural uncertainties in ocean models regarding eddy parameterization vs eddy-resolving dynamics alter regional response to freshwater fluxes.
Sparse and uncertain historical observations of ice shelf basal melt fluxes, especially prior to 1990 and post-2016.
Persistent CMIP6 multi-model biases in Southern Ocean SST trends and Antarctic sea ice trends.
extraction_notes: The paper is supported by the NSF STC LEAP computational resources (Award 2019625) and utilizes LEAP-Pangeo infrastructure to analyze CMIP6 data, but does not train or evaluate machine learning models.
